title: Make the cards the main event
question: Choose the visual world for the full redesign. All paths include a calmer home, a held hand, visible turn direction, a real countdown, automatic forced penalties, and stronger card motion and sound.

options.label: After-hours arcade
options.lineage: Night-time arcade title screens and shared card nights
options.thesis: A quiet plum stage makes every card throw, reverse and penalty the star.
options.viewport: Compact UNO wordmark, three opponents around a clear central pile, direction chevrons and an amber 24s turn ring; a held fan fills the bottom.
options.risk: Too dark would feel severe; keep faces bright and controls friendly.

raised.raise: A single clear center, with every turn effect choreographed around it.
Make accumulated penalties feel physically heavier without changing the deck.
Each action gets one visible beginning, landing and handoff.
Keep the whole composition readable at small sizes.
One dominant focal point, with secondary content genuinely quiet.
Only real state receives accent color; leave and reset remain separated.

options.label: Color court
options.lineage: Friendly recreational courts and modern casual games
options.thesis: A warm, open playing field gives the game a bright, welcoming rhythm.
options.viewport: Quiet ivory home with one yellow Play control; inside a muted teal court, opponents and piles gather closely above a generous held hand.
options.risk: The familiar casual-game direction; distinction depends on excellent card handling.

options.label: Garden choreography
options.thesis: Garden axes would become fixed player positions and sequential water cues would become card effects.
options.viewport: Garden axes would become fixed player positions and sequential water cues would become card effects; formal gardens lose both social familiarity and action clarity.
options.case: Garden axes would become fixed player positions and sequential water cues would become card effects; formal gardens lose both social familiarity and action clarity.
options.kept: A single clear center, with every turn effect choreographed around it.
options.risk: Formal geometry could make a casual card night feel ceremonial.

options.label: Coiled earth
options.thesis: Coil bands could carry penalty accumulation.
options.viewport: Coil bands could carry penalty accumulation; clay loses both native-card recognition and instant turn clarity.
options.case: Coil bands could carry penalty accumulation; clay loses both native-card recognition and instant turn clarity.
options.kept: Make accumulated penalties feel physically heavier without changing the deck.
options.risk: Clay material also recalls a previously rejected toy-like direction.

options.label: Safelight sequence
options.thesis: Fixed development stations could frame draw, play and hand.
options.viewport: Fixed development stations could frame draw, play and hand; photographic chemistry loses social recognition and introduces a false sequence.
options.case: Fixed development stations could frame draw, play and hand; photographic chemistry loses social recognition and introduces a false sequence.
options.kept: Each action gets one visible beginning, landing and handoff.
options.risk: Amber-only imagery would weaken the four-color game.

options.label: Miniature room
options.thesis: Room objects could host Play and Friends.
options.viewport: Room objects could host Play and Friends; an isometric room loses both compactness and immediate card focus for this brief.
options.case: Room objects could host Play and Friends; an isometric room loses both compactness and immediate card focus for this brief.
options.kept: Keep the whole composition readable at small sizes.
options.risk: Decorative furnishings repeat the clutter the owner rejected.

options.label: Printed issue
options.thesis: A masthead and two columns could hold play and rooms.
options.viewport: A masthead and two columns could hold play and rooms; editorial reading loses both game energy and immediacy.
options.case: A masthead and two columns could hold play and rooms; editorial reading loses both game energy and immediacy.
options.kept: One dominant focal point, with secondary content genuinely quiet.
options.risk: A magazine can feel like a landing page instead of a game.

options.label: Graphite console
options.thesis: Persistent panels could show hand, turn and history.
options.viewport: Persistent panels could show hand, turn and history; work-console grammar loses playful identification and makes a single turn harder to scan.
options.case: Persistent panels could show hand, turn and history; work-console grammar loses playful identification and makes a single turn harder to scan.
options.kept: Only real state receives accent color; leave and reset remain separated.
options.risk: Tiled panels would turn the game into the dashboard being removed.

canonCard.label: Classic casual-game arena
canonCard.thesis: The familiar bright blue card-game screen, executed with care.
canonCard.viewport: Centered Play on home; a clean blue multiplayer arena, corner identities, obvious countdown and bottom-held hand.
canonCard.risk: Intentionally conventional; it may feel similar to other online card games.
